definitions.explanation: A condition or circumstance that puts one in a worse position.

examples.japanese: この{条件|じょうけん}は{我々|われわれ}に{不利|ふり}だ。
examples.english: These conditions are disadvantageous to us.

examples.japanese: {不利|ふり}な{立場|たちば}に{立|た}たされた。
examples.english: I was put in a disadvantageous position.

examples.japanese: {被告|ひこく}に{不利|ふり}な{証拠|しょうこ}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: Evidence unfavorable to the defendant came out.

notes:
{不利|ふり} describes situations, conditions, or positions that work against someone's interests. It functions as both a noun and na-adjective.

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {不利|ふり}な{条件|じょうけん} (unfavorable conditions)
- Predicate: 〜に{不利|ふり}だ (to be disadvantageous to ~)
- Noun: {不利|ふり}を{被|こうむ}る (to suffer a disadvantage)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不利|ふり}な{立場|たちば}: disadvantageous position
- {不利|ふり}な{状況|じょうきょう}: unfavorable situation
- {不利|ふり}な{証拠|しょうこ}: incriminating evidence
- {不利|ふり}に{働|はたら}く: to work against (someone)

RELATED:
- {不利益|ふりえき}: disadvantage, harm (noun)
- Antonym: {有利|ゆうり} (advantageous, favorable)
